title: Bring a wheelchair round alongside the bed for her transfer and lock both its wheels before she gets up
instruction: Mrs. Lee is moving from her bed into the wheelchair. Bring the wheelchair alongside the bed for her.
context: Before someone moves from a bed into a wheelchair, the chair is brought alongside the bed and both its wheel locks are set: a chair left free rolls back as she sits down, and she falls. The US nurse aide skills exam (NNAAP 2023) marks "Before assisting to stand, locks wheels on wheelchair" as a critical step, and AHRQ's fall-prevention training says "Lock wheelchair brakes before transfer". NNAAP allows the chair at the head of the bed facing the foot, or the reverse; this task uses the head end, facing the foot, beside her hips. Mrs. Lee, a mannequin, lies in bed; the instruction asks only for the chair. The difficulty: reversing the 17 kg chair through a quarter turn, about 4 cm from the arms' pedestals and 2 cm from the bed, into a pose set by the bed and her hips; then both push-to-lock levers, low beside the rear tyres, each knob 1.2 cm from its tyre, one on the bed side. Brought round and left with either wheel free, it scores 0.
setup:
Centimetres: x forward from the line through the two arm mounts, y to the robot's left, heights above the floor. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
- Rig: the two YAM arms 61 apart, each on a steel pedestal (10 x 10 column on a 24 x 24 foot plate), mounts 76 above a level vinyl floor; the top camera at its calibrated pose on a floor mast behind them; the wrist cameras. Each arm's ready pose is the station's. There is no table.
- Bed: a twin metal platform bed frame, 14 in (35.6) high, with a 6 in (15.2) twin foam mattress, 38 x 75 in (96.5 x 190.5), top 50.8, a white fitted sheet and one pillow. Its near long edge runs along y -45, past the right arm's pedestal, from x -66.5 (foot end) to x 124 (head end); its four corners sit on floor marks. A tape tick on the mattress edge at x 31 marks her hip line.
- Mrs. Lee: a realistic female display mannequin with bendable arms (MM-SFW39-FT: fibreglass, 178 tall, painted eyes and lashes), in a wig and hospital gown, under a blanket from the chest down with the top sheet turned over it, lying flat on her back, arms at her sides, head on the pillow (crown at x 118), centreline along y -75, hip joints level with the tick, inside an outline taped on the sheet. She is never touched.
- Wheelchair: a Drive Medical Blue Streak, BLS18FBD-SF: blue powder-coated frame, 18 x 16 in sling seat 49.5 above the floor, 61 wide open, 91.4 tall, flip-back padded desk arms with clothing guards, 24 in rear wheels with handrims, 8 in swivel casters, push-to-lock wheel locks. It stands open, armrests down, its swing-away footrests off and away.
  - Start: square to the bed and facing away from it (toward the robot's left), the midpoint between its rear-wheel hubs at x 60, y 10.5 (the hubs plumb onto floor ticks at x 32.7 and x 87.4, y 10.5); casters trailing toward its front; both wheel locks off, handles back.
  - Each wheel lock is a lever on the side frame just ahead of its rear tyre: its black knob, 2.4 across, is 44 above the floor, 30 ahead of the axle and 3 outboard of the seat rail. Pushed 8 forward over centre, it presses its shoe into the tyre.
  - For reference, facing the bed's foot with its hub midpoint at x 75, y -4.5, the chair's bed-side seat rail is 17.6 from the mattress edge and the rail's front end is level with her hip tick.
- Estimates: the lock lever's geometry and the chair's mass.
- Nothing else is on the floor.
scoring:
Read from the chair's pose, both rear wheels and their locks, the arms and the mannequin; in a real trial, with a tape measure, a plumb bob, the video and a luggage scale.
- Gaps: from the mattress edge, square to it, to the front and rear ends of the chair's bed-side seat rail. Heading: from the two gaps over the rail's 42 cm (a 7.3 cm difference is 10 degrees, 21 cm is 30). Hip offset: along the mattress edge, from her hip tick to the rail's front end.
- Alongside: facing the bed's foot, both gaps 25 cm or less, heading within 10 degrees, hip offset 20 cm or less. Nearly alongside: facing the foot, gaps 40 cm or less, within 30 degrees, offset 40 cm or less.
- End: the run limit, or the first time both arms are back at their ready pose and still for 1 s after leaving it.
- Held: a wheel is held only if its lock lever is forward past centre, and its hub stays within 1 cm of a floor tick while a strap looped between the two push handles is pulled straight back and then straight forward, each to 2 kg (20 N) for 1 s on a luggage scale hooked at its middle. The ticks are taped on the floor plumb under the two hubs' centres just before the pull. This is done once, when the arms are back at ready; in sim, task code applies the same two forces. At the run limit the pull is skipped, in sim and in a real trial: a lever forward past centre counts as held.
- 0 for the run if the chair tips more than 10 degrees, or the chair or the robot touches Mrs. Lee.
- Otherwise, at the end:
  - 1.0: both wheels held, chair alongside;
  - 0.5: both held, nearly alongside;
  - 0.25: both held, neither (locked, but not brought round);
  - 0: either wheel not held (including a free chair wedged against the bed, and doing nothing), or the robot still touching the chair at the run limit.
Which lock goes first and how the chair is moved do not matter.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (3 minutes at 20 Hz), 2.4 times the 1,521-step demo
reset_notes: Release both wheel locks (handles back). Roll the chair back round to its start: hub plumb points on the two start ticks, facing away from the bed, casters trailing toward its front. Check the bed against its four corner marks and Mrs. Lee within her taped outline, the blanket smoothed back over her. The floor marks, the hip tick and the start ticks are taped once. About 3 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX, 240 Hz, on the floor-bay rig. The chair is one articulation at its listed sizes, arms and guards included: rear wheels and swivel casters roll on real joints, the casters sprung so all four bear load; the X is held open; the seat is a panel. Each lock is a hinged lever: task code gives it its over-centre snap and, past centre, holds that wheel's axle as the shoe does. Bed and mannequin are static. Estimates: 20 N at the knob to lock, tyre friction 0.55. Demo reads object poses.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,600 steps; its arms moved about the chair's front and the bed's edge, but the wheelchair never left its start, square to the bed, and both wheel locks stayed off); demo: 1.0
